definitions.explanation: The soft, faint light around dawn or dusk when the sun is below the horizon; also used for any dim, ambient light.

examples.japanese: {薄明|はくめい}の{中|なか}を{歩|ある}く。
{薄明|はくめい}の{空|そら}が{美|うつく}しかった。
{夜明|よあ}け{前|まえ}の{薄明|はくめい}の{時間帯|じかんたい}は、{鳥|とり}たちが{一斉|いっせい}に{鳴|な}き{始|はじ}める。
examples.english: In the twilight hours before dawn, the birds all begin singing at once.

notes:
A compound of {薄|はく} (thin, faint) and {明|めい} (light, brightness). A literary and somewhat formal word for the soft light of dawn or dusk. It has a poetic, atmospheric quality and is often used in literature, photography, and descriptions of nature.

In astronomy, {薄明|はくめい} is also a technical term for twilight — the period when the sun is below the horizon but its light is still scattered in the atmosphere.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {薄明|はくめい}の{空|そら}: twilight sky
- {薄明|はくめい}の{中|なか}: in the twilight
- {薄明|はくめい}の{光|ひかり}: twilight light
- {朝|あさ}の{薄明|はくめい}: morning twilight

SIMILAR WORDS:
- たそがれ: twilight (especially dusk) — more poetic and literary; from {黄昏|たそがれ}
- {夕暮|ゆうぐ}れ: evening twilight, dusk — more everyday and specific to evening
- {明|あ}け{方|がた}: dawn, daybreak — the time just before sunrise
- {薄明|うすあか}るい: dimly lit — the adjective describing the quality of faint light
